question: Do accessible sources identify Malolos inland and brackish watercourses or provide fish evidence that can be safely assigned to species and waterbody records?

officialWatercourseContext.lccapLocator: Section A.2.1, Climate Change and Disaster Risk Profile
officialWatercourseContext.lccapFinding: The City of Malolos Enhanced Local Climate Change Action Plan 2023–2032 names Pamarawan, Galas, Malaway, Pangagtan, and Bugwan rivers.
officialWatercourseContext.drrmLocator: City Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Plan 2022–2026, Section 1.4 Environmental Sector, subsection 1.4.2 Tributaries
officialWatercourseContext.drrmFinding: The official city-hosted DRRM plan contains a tributary table naming 11 rivers and all 15 creeks, with source-reported drain-area barangay labels. It corroborates all 26 normalized watercourse names in the third-party Ecological Profile copy, subject to two spelling variants noted below. Neither official plan provides fish survey data or channel geometry.

thirdPartyWatercourseInventory.finding: The reviewed third-party copy lists 11 rivers and 15 creeks (26 names total), with barangay labels described as drain areas. A City-hosted 2022–2026 DRRM plan lists the same 11 rivers and all 15 creeks, although the tributary table continues across a page. A bounded search did not locate the Ecological Profile itself on the city website; this does not prove that an official copy does not exist.
thirdPartyWatercourseInventory.officialComparison: All 26 normalized watercourse names in the third-party profile copy are also listed in the official DRRM tributary table. The official plan prints “Apulid - Malangam Creek” while the profile copy prints “Apulid - Malanggam Creek”; the official table splits “Guin h awa” while the profile copy prints “Guinhawa”. The official table continues after the page break to include the last four creeks.

watercourses.interpretation: The city-hosted DRRM plan provides source-reported names and drain-area barangay labels for all 11 rivers and 15 creeks also listed in the third-party Ecological Profile copy. Differences are typographic variants for Apulid-Malangam/Malang(g)am and Guinhawa; the tributary table continues across a page, which explains why the first extraction showed only 11 creek rows. The barangay labels are not independently verified hydrological crosswalks. Neither table establishes channel geometry, aliases, flow connectivity, or a fish inventory.

catchStatistics.attributedOffice: Office of the City Agriculturist (CAgO), as credited in the third-party copy

entries.printedTitle: Local Fish Catch in In-Land Water, 2023
Local Fish Catch in Municipal Water, 2023

catchStatistics.finding: The tables report aggregate totals by barangay, but no taxa, fish-specific methods, catch coordinates, or allocation to named waterways. Totals are retained as unverified document context only and must not be presented as species occurrences, current abundance, or river-specific catch.

speciesEvidence.interpretation: Neither reviewed source supplies taxon-level evidence that can be assigned to a named Malolos watercourse. The aggregate catch tables do not establish presence, absence, abundance, catchability, diet, or safety.

fishSurveySearchLead.candidateTitle: Morphometric Traits of Ichthyofauna in Malolos District Rivers, Bulacan, Philippines Year 2021
searches: Title search restricted to the named school website and DepEd domains
fishSurveySearchLead.documentAsHosted: Third-party Scribd user-uploaded Module 4 Answer Sheet; the relevant section is embedded among Practical Research 2 classroom exercises. Uploader identity is not used to establish authorship.
reviewedTextSignals: The surrounding assignment instructs the student to propose a research title and write a background of study.
The ichthyofauna text describes an objective and asks what fish species would be collected; it does not provide a species list, sampling results, or fish measurements.
fishSurveySearchLead.disposition: Unverified proposal/classroom exercise, not a completed fish survey. Do not cite as occurrence or inventory evidence. The bounded official-domain search found no hosted results copy; that does not prove none exists.

accessAndReuse.decision: Record source citations and concise facts only. Do not reproduce the profile tables/maps or project catch totals into public app data. Seek an official profile copy and an independently reusable, taxon-resolved fish survey.

nextActions: Search for an official City of Malolos Ecological Profile and verify the table provenance, version, and fishery definitions before relying on the third-party copy.

Search repositories and primary literature for taxon-resolved Malolos or named-watercourse surveys with dates, methods, station/locality precision, vouchers or diagnostic evidence, and item-specific reuse terms; retrieve an original completed study if one exists behind the unverified classroom proposal.
Resolve names, tributary relationships, barangay associations, and channel geometry using authoritative hydrography data before assigning a reach or locality.
Keep aquaculture, stocking, market, and aggregate catch statistics separate from wild river occurrence records; keep Central Luzon and Luzon incomplete.

sources.supports: Official city-hosted DRRM tributary table lists all 11 rivers and 15 creeks with source-reported drain-area barangay labels; no fish inventory or channel geometry.
Official city-hosted climate plan corroborates five of the 11 named rivers.
Third-party copy lists the same 11 rivers and 15 creeks plus aggregate catch tables; no taxa or watercourse-specific catch allocation.
